auth.profile.language.title: Language
auth.profile.language.description: Applies to everything the panel writes, including the messages it generates while you are not looking at it.
auth.signIn.title: Sign in
auth.signIn.footer: Accounts are created by the platform operator. If you cannot get in and the message above does not say why, ask them to check whether your account is suspended.
auth.challenge.title: Confirm it is you
auth.challenge.promptAuthenticator: Open your authenticator app and enter the current six-digit code.
auth.challenge.promptRecovery: Enter one of the recovery codes you saved when you turned this on.
auth.challenge.hintAuthenticator: Codes change every 30 seconds. If yours keeps being rejected, check that your phone’s clock is set automatically.
auth.challenge.hintRecovery: Ten characters, written with a hyphen in the middle. Each one works once.
auth.challenge.noRecoveryLeft: You have no recovery codes left. If you cannot reach your authenticator, the platform operator has to turn the second factor off for you.
auth.profile.title: Profile
auth.profile.description: Your name, your password, and the facts the panel records about this account.
auth.profile.nameDesc: The name appears next to anything you do in the panel and in the audit log.
auth.profile.emailNotice: This is also your sign-in name. Ask the platform operator if it needs to change.
auth.profile.passwordNeverChanged: Never - still the one you were given
auth.password.title: Password
auth.password.description: Changing it signs out every other browser you are signed in to. This one stays.
auth.password.hint: At least {min} characters. A few unrelated words is easier to remember and harder to guess than a short one with symbols in it.
auth.security.title: Security
auth.security.description: Everything that decides who can get into {email}.
auth.totp.title: Two-factor authentication
auth.totp.descOn: Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator after your password.
auth.totp.descOff: A code from your phone on top of your password. It is the single change that most reduces the chance of somebody else getting into this account.
auth.totp.descPending: Add the secret to your authenticator, then type the code it shows. Nothing is switched on until that code verifies.
auth.totp.offNotice: Turning it off discards your recovery codes as well. Your password is required, because this is the change worth taking an account for.
auth.totp.qrAria: QR code containing the setup secret for this account
auth.totp.qrScanNotice: Scan this from a second device. On the phone you are reading this on, use the button above instead.
auth.totp.secretExplanation: Time-based, SHA-1, six digits, thirty seconds - the defaults every authenticator uses. Spaces in the secret are for reading; type it without them if your app objects.
auth.totp.pendingWarning: Setup was started but never finished, and the QR code is only ever shown once. If it is already in your authenticator, enter a code below. Otherwise start again to get a new one - the old secret stops working the moment you do.
auth.totp.startAgain: Start again with a new secret
auth.recovery.title: Recovery codes
auth.recovery.description: What gets you in when the phone with the authenticator on it is not available. Each code works once.
auth.recovery.saveNow: Save these now. They are not shown again, and any previous codes have stopped working.
auth.recovery.allUsed: All {count} of your codes have been used. Generate a new batch before you need one.
auth.recovery.regenerateNotice: Generating a new batch immediately invalidates the old one.
auth.recovery.turnOnFirst: Turn on two-factor authentication first. Codes are issued as part of that, and there is nothing for them to recover from until then.
auth.sessions.title: Signed-in browsers
auth.sessions.description: Anything you do not recognise should be signed out, and then your password changed.
auth.sessions.emptyDesc: Nothing is signed in to this account right now, including this page - which means the session behind it has just expired. Reload to sign in again.
auth.sessions.confirmBody: {count} other session will end on its next request. This browser stays signed in.
auth.sessions.confirmBodyPlural: {count} other sessions will end on its next request. This browser stays signed in.
auth.sessions.btnNoOther: No other browsers to sign out
auth.sessions.note: This browser is left alone. The others are signed out on their next request.
auth.sessions.useSignOut: Use “Sign out” in the account menu to end this one.
auth.tokens.title: API tokens
auth.tokens.description: A bearer token for /api/v1. It acts as you, inside the permissions you give it.
auth.tokens.cardDesc: Revoked and expired ones are kept so you can tell what a call in the audit log came from.
auth.tokens.emptyDesc: Create one above when something other than a browser needs to reach the panel - a deployment pipeline, a backup script, your own tooling.
auth.tokens.bannerCopyPrompt: Copy it now. This is the only time it is shown - if you lose it, revoke this token and issue another.
auth.tokens.bannerFooter: Send it as an Authorization: Bearer header. Put it in your deployment tool’s secret store, not in a repository.
auth.tokens.newCardDesc: A token acts as you, limited to the permissions and the organization you give it here. Every call it makes is recorded in the audit log against its name.
auth.tokens.noOrgMessage: You are not a member of any organization yet, and a token has to act in one. Accept an invitation first, and this form will work.
auth.tokens.name: Name
auth.tokens.nameHint: What you will recognise it by in this list a year from now.
auth.tokens.orgHintUnscoped: Leave it blank for a token that is not tied to one tenant. Only a platform operator may do that.
auth.tokens.orgHintScoped: The token can only act inside this organization.
auth.tokens.permissionsHint: Give it the least it needs. Read and write are separate on purpose.
auth.tokens.expiresDaysHint: Up to {max}. Leave it blank for a token that never expires - a short life is one fewer secret to have left lying around.
auth.tokens.revokeNotice: Anything using this token stops working straight away, and it cannot be brought back.
auth.admin.title: Accounts
auth.admin.description: Everyone who can sign in to this installation. There is no public sign-up, so this page is the only way in.
auth.admin.singleOperatorWarning: One active operator. If that account is lost, nobody can administer the platform - promote a second one.
auth.admin.emptyMatchDesc: No account's name or address contains “{query}”. Clear the filter to see all {total}.
auth.admin.lastOperatorNotice: The last operator who can still sign in. Promote somebody else first, or nobody will be able to administer the platform.
auth.admin.suspendConfirmBody: They cannot sign in, and every session they have is ended on its next request. Their projects keep running.
auth.admin.createDesc: Tell them the password over something that is not this panel, and ask them to change it on their first sign-in.
auth.admin.firstPasswordHint: At least {min} characters, and at most 72 bytes - past that, BCrypt stops reading.
auth.admin.copyPasswordDesc: Copy the first password for this account
auth.admin.roleAdmin: Platform operator - every tenant, every node
auth.admin.roleHint: An operator can reach every organization, every node and the audit log. Give it to as few people as the platform can be run with.
